newsitem.title: UK: DLR WEAKER AS BUBA INFLATION WARNING BOOSTS MARK.
newsitem.headline: DLR WEAKER AS BUBA INFLATION WARNING BOOSTS MARK.

text.p: The dollar was under pressure after a hawkish assessment about German inflation from the Bundesbank boosted the mark across the board, traders said.

In its August monthly report the German central bank said it could not be overlooked that there had been a stronger rise in consumer prices in recent months and it would orientate its policy so that price stability could be maintained.
This was seen as increasing the chances of a German interest rate rise.
The central bank also said it will observe further currency rate movements closely with a view to the risks presented for price stability.

"The assertion that the exchange rate is very significant in policy decisions, the fact that they highlight the recent rise in some inflation figures and the desire to see M3 growth lower suggest that they may be closer to a rate increase than previously thought," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist at Bank of America in London.
At 0708 GMT the dollar was at 1.8535/45 marks, off a session low at 1.8514 but down from 1.8638/48 late here on Tuesday. Against the yen, it stood at 116.26/36 yen, up from 115.95/116.00.
Dollar/yen shed ground from an overnight high at 116.75 yen, tracking dollar/mark lower but found a prop ahead of firm support at 116.00.
Germany's July consumer inflation rose to 1.9 percent, data released on Tuesday showed, the highest level since June 1995 and up from 1.7 percent in June.

Though the CPI was boosted by one-off factors last month, economists expect it to rise above 2.0 percent soon, the level regarded as acceptable by the Bundesbank. Germany's import prices, due later this month, are also key for signs of whether the mark's weakness is boosting inflation.
Meanwhile, German July wholesale prices dropped 1.0 percent from the previous month - at the upper end of market expectations - but were up 2.0 percent from a year ago.
The response of the U.S. Treasury market to retail sales data and producer price data for July, due at 1230 GMT, will be key for the dollar today, traders said.

"There are worries in the U.S. bond market about rising inflation - and at the same time expectations that German interest rates will increase. That combination should keep the dollar fairly steady for now unless today's data upset the markets," said David Bloom, FX strategist at HSBC James Capel.

Even though dollar/yen suffered with dollar/mark, dealers said it had a better chance of picking up steam. The yen weakened against the mark overnight as the mark pushed through firm resistance at 62.60/70 on short-covering and stop-loss buying. It also weakened against the Australian dollar.
"It's quite difficult to see the yen rally significantly," said Bloom. "People are worried about the economy and think there won't be a rate increase within the next six months."
Eisuke Sakakibara, Japan's vice-minister for international affairs is scheduled to meet U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers in Washington on Wednesday.
Mark/yen was at 62.82/85, up from 62.24/27. The mark has recovered from two-year lows just above 62 yen on Monday.
